text:
alex_ops: Heads-up — starting 10:42 UTC we saw a spike in GPU errors in us-west1. Error-rate up ~6x, capacity showing ~18% unavailable across rack-11 -> rack-14. Seeing both soft ECCs and sporadic Xid 13/31 patterns. :warning:

sana_infra: On it. Are these correlated with the nightly provisioning window?

alex_ops: Not the window — this is steady since 10:42. No deploys. Telemetry shows higher CE counts and an increase in kernel Xid logs.

lee_sre: Pulled the probes. NVLink pings OK but card telemetry shows intermittent memory-correction bursts. Attaching tail of dmesg from a node: 

```
[10:43:12] NVRM: Xid (31): GPU has fallen off the bus
[10:43:13] kernel: nvidia: NVRM: GPU 0000:81:00:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[10:43:15] EDAC MC0: CE error: GPU mem error corrected
[10:44:01] NVRM: Xid (13): Ecc multi-bit detect
```

lee_sre: Looks like multi-bit ECC detection -> intermittent resets.

jess_prod: Impact: a few host pools hit degraded and model routing triggered fallback. Production latency up ~40ms p50 on text-gen routes; cost spike because fallbacks are larger models in other pools. We should avoid broad drains until we have per-card confirmation.

mike_platform: Agree. Suggest throttling allocation to the affected racks and enable routing to dedicated pools in eu-west1/us-east1. We can also open an emergency ticket with spot provider for hardware replacement.

alex_ops: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Mark rack-11..14 as limited for scheduling (soft-drain) 2) Pin higher-risk jobs away 3) Route new requests off these racks 4) Run remote diag script to collect nvml logs / memtests. Anyone object?

lee_sre: No objections. I'll run the diag. Command I'll use: 

```
for n in $(nodes -r rack-11..14); do ssh $n "sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-diag --nvml --memtest 5m" & done
```

sana_infra: Doing soft-drain now via redwoodctl to avoid kubectl churn: 

```
redwoodctl node update --rack rack-11 --sched-state drain-soft --reason "elevated ECC/Xid"
```

sana_infra: Also bumped the routing policy to prefer dedicated/us-east1 for latency-sensitive routes. :arrow_right:

deploy-bot: automatic-routing-change: policy applied to route group "text-gen-low-latency" -> prefer dedicated/us-east1 (started at 10:55 UTC).

ci-bot: alert-notification: Pager duty triggered for eng-sre team (severity: high) — alert id pd-77421.

jess_prod: Quick cost note: expected delta ~+6% on hourly bill while routes shift. Approving given severity.

lee_sre: Diag results coming back: two nodes show persistent single-card memory ECC growth + one node with recurring Xid 31. Memtest passed short runs but NVML reports increased corrected counts. Looks like early bit-flip cascade, hardware replacement recommended.

alex_ops: OK. Plan: schedule RMA for affected cards (3 cards). For ramp: keep soft-drain until replacement; if more nodes degrade, escalate to hard-drain and preemptively reprovision from spare pool.

mike_platform: I've reserved 3 warm spares in us-west1-pool-B and started pre-warming images. If we need hot-swap, we can reprovision within 12-18m.

sana_infra: Will track in ticket INF-7442 and attach NVML dumps. Setting owner: lee_sre.

lee_sre: Monitoring graph queries added: 

```
sum(rate(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) by (rack)
sum(rate(nvidia_xid_errors[5m])) by (rack)
```
I'll alert if any rack exceeds 2x current baseline.

alex_ops: Thanks. Follow-ups: - Replace 3 cards (RMA) - Keep soft-drain until healthy - Continue routing to dedicated pools - Postmortem if capacity loss >20% or >30m impact.

jess_prod: Noted. I'll send a brief customer-facing banner through infra-status if impact persists >30m.

lee_sre: Adding final note: this looks like early-stage bit-flip chatter, might be correlated with a vendor microcode change last month. I'll cross-check firmware versions and file to INF-7442. :eyes:

alex_ops: Great. Closing triage for now; will update thread with RMA times and any hard-drain decisions. :thumbsup:"
